clue.text: Local atheist, according to Spooner, who worked in the White House

definitions.text: who worked in the White House

indicators.note: naming the Reverend Spooner says the opening sounds of the two words are traded

parts.note: a local is a resident of a place
a pagan, loosely, is someone without the mainstream faith

explanation.surface: A godless neighbour is said to have once worked at the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose sound swap: the P that opens PAGAN is moved to the front of RESIDENT, and the R takes its place, giving PRESIDENT and REAGAN (pay-gan becomes ray-gan).
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan held the US presidency, so he worked from its official residence in Washington.

clue.text: Insulting poor poor nun — this could be her

parts.note: a personal remark is an insulting one

indicators.note: poor here means badly formed, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is being rude about a nun in reduced circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'poor' is the anagram signal working on the second 'poor' plus NUN, which gives PRONOUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'her' is one example of a pronoun standing for a particular person, the grammatical class of I, you, him.

clue.text: Clean around top of teapot's spout

indicators.note: around turns the word for clean the other way round

parts.note: clean means pure

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning a teapot's spout, starting at the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to gush out forcefully, as a volcano or fountain does.

clue.text: Where Hugh Laurie's seen not using outsiders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Hugh Laurie starred in the TV drama House, so he is seen in it
second meaning: done within an organisation by its own staff

explanation.walkthrough: House was the American medical drama in which the British actor Hugh Laurie played Dr Gregory House.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done within a company by its own employees, rather than contracted out, is described this way.

clue.text: For example, Krypton Factor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: krypton is a chemical ...
second meaning: a component or contributing part

explanation.walkthrough: The Krypton Factor was a British TV quiz show, which disguises the split between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is a noble gas on the periodic table, and a factor is a constituent part of something.

clue.text: Firm about working later this evening

indicators.note: about means the word for firm goes around the other piece

parts.note: firm means tight, as a firm grip
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A company is getting on with business late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to the night of the present day, the coming evening hours.

clue.text: He performed with Lake poet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Keith ... played in the rock band ..., Lake and Palmer
second meaning: Ralph Waldo ..., the American poet and essayist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake poet' suggests Wordsworth and the Lake District poets, but the clue splits after Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a prog-rock keyboardist and to the nineteenth-century transcendentalist writer.

clue.text: Sponsor to follow up yearly fee

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
PA is per annum, Latin for yearly
rent is a fee paid for use of property

explanation.surface: A sponsor chases up an annual payment.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism a godparent stands sponsor for the child, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Telegraph pole? Hastings has one

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pole-like column in a newspaper such as the Telegraph
second meaning: the journalist Max Hastings writes a regular piece in the press

explanation.walkthrough: A telegraph pole carries wires, but here the Telegraph is the newspaper and a pole is a column; Hastings is the journalist, not the battle site.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular article slot in a paper is called this, and columnists like Max Hastings fill one.

clue.text: Inelegant collar delivered when out

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar

indicators.note: out means the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A clumsy collar was brought round when someone was not at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roughly shaped and unrefined, like timber cut crudely with an axe, lacks polish.

clue.text: Pay for edge over wicket

parts.note: an edge is an end
O stands for over on cricket scorecards
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary line: a nick off the edge and a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a positional instruction but is a cricket letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow something such as a college chair is to fund it with money.

clue.text: Old boy, essentially impertinent and vulgar, gets stick out

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of impertinent
vulgar means rude

explanation.surface: A cheeky, crude former pupil is handed a beating with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to protrude or push forward noticeably, the way something sticking out does.

clue.text: Light chatter with city politician

parts.note: gas is idle talk
LA is Los Angeles
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Easy conversation with a local councillor.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp burning coal gas, as in Victorian streets, is a source of illumination.

clue.text: Certainly not beginning to heckle Japanese drama

parts.note: a firm refusal is no

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of heckle

explanation.surface: A plea not to start shouting abuse at a Japanese play.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is the classical masked theatre form of Japan, dating from the fourteenth century.

clue.text: Power nap, and something to lean on

parts.note: arm means power or might, as in the long arm of the law
a nap is a rest

explanation.surface: A quick snooze followed by a comfortable support.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised side of a chair supports the elbow, giving a place to rest your weight.

clue.text: Somewhere in the Alps, flash TV chef eating nougat on vacation

indicators.note: eating means the outer words take in the other letters

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
Raymond Blanc is a French chef known from British television

indicators.note: emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of nougat

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef on holiday in the Alps munches nougat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps, on the French-Italian border.

clue.text: When tipping, almost mislaid Peruvian coin

indicators.note: tipping over in a down clue turns the letters upside down
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something mislaid is lost

explanation.surface: Someone nearly loses a coin while leaving a tip in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: The sol is the currency unit of Peru, its name meaning sun in Spanish.

clue.text: Prepare to drive across centre of Barnsley to get contract

indicators.note: across means the golfing phrase spans the other letters

parts.note: a golfer tees up before driving

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: middle two letters of Barnsley

explanation.surface: A golfer gets ready to drive through Barnsley, a Yorkshire town, to sign a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles that contract tighten, becoming taut, which is the phrasal verb here.

clue.text: Shell-like fruit, not soft

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
P is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: Some fruit with a shell that is hard, not soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell-like' is British slang for an ear, from its shape: 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer ear's curved shape resembles a seashell, giving rise to this informal British term.

clue.text: Socially distanced writers hit back after confinement

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for confining animals

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a slap is a hit

explanation.surface: Writers kept apart in lockdown strike back after being confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondents who write letters to each other without ever meeting are distant friends.

clue.text: Man demonstrating tap in Holiday Inn?

definitions.text: Man demonstrating tap in Holiday Inn?

parts.words: Man demonstrating tap in Holiday Inn?
parts.note: the 1942 film Holiday Inn featured a famous tap-dancing star, not a plumber in a hotel

explanation.walkthrough: A man showing off a tap in a hotel sounds like a plumber; Holiday Inn is the 1942 musical in which Fred Astaire danced opposite Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the celebrated dancer who performed tap routines in the musical film Holiday Inn.

clue.text: Casanova secured buckles

indicators.note: something that buckles is bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous lover fastens his belt buckles.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is a byword for a womaniser who lures lovers.

clue.text: Producer about to interrupt Rocky actor

indicators.note: to interrupt means the short word breaks into the other letters
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A film producer is about to cut in on the actor from Rocky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky actor' suggests Sylvester Stallone, but Rocky is the anagram signal and the actor is just five letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A creator is one who makes or brings something into being, a maker.

clue.text: Impulse to fix staple?

parts.note: to cap a price is to fix its limit
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A sudden urge to set the price of a basic commodity.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim or unaccountable change of mind.

clue.text: Adaptable, the Spanish clubs stocking Italian wine

indicators.note: stocking means holding the wine inside, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
C is clubs in card games
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: Spanish clubs flexibly keeping Italian wine on their shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic in its figurative sense means flexible, able to stretch to fit circumstances.

clue.text: Age Fitzgerald's written about

indicators.note: the letters are written about, inside, the name that holds them

explanation.surface: A period that F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote about, the Jazz Age.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Fitzgerald's Jazz Age, but the answer sits inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a historical period, which an age also is.

clue.text: Circled right piece in dictionary

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the dictionary's letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
R is right
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Someone ringed the correct entry in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite that orbited a planet travelled round it in a loop.

clue.text: Fake doctor passes out? Cop able to revive

indicators.note: reviving the letters brings them back in a new form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A bogus doctor faints, and a policeman can bring him round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake doctor' looks like a quack, but the definition is the sham pill a doctor hands out.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert dummy medicine given out as if it were real treatment.

clue.text: Tree resin rising in lime leaf

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sap from a lime tree climbs up into its foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum obtained from tropical trees, used in varnish and incense.

clue.text: African resident fine with au pair appearing only occasionally

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: only occasional letters show, every other one

parts.note: alternate letters of au pair

explanation.surface: A satisfactory home help from Africa who only turns up now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a giraffe relative native to the rainforests of the Congo.

clue.text: Before short trek, make up a posh liqueur

indicators.note: before places the invented word ahead of the shortened walk

parts.note: to coin a word is to make it up

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Before a quick hike, someone invents a smart liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured spirit, a type of triple sec.

clue.text: Greek character with clarinet and Corea playing fusion?

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: playing suggests letters set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek musician on clarinet jamming with Chick Corea in a jazz-fusion style.
explanation.walkthrough: Chick Corea was a jazz-fusion pianist, which makes 'fusion' look musical; the question mark flags it as an example of the physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusion in physics, the merging of atomic nuclei as in the sun, is one kind of atomic process.
